title: Grateful Dead Live at Oregon State University on 1970-01-17
lineage: Master Soundboard Reel > DAT > CDR > SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with occasional distortion but very listenable; the show shines with standout performances of Good Lovin', Mason’s Children, Dark Star and a powerful The Eleven.
ai_review.review: The early‑1970 capture from Corvallis delivers a fun, organ‑rich vibe (a ‘67‑style Hammond that even came from a Baptist church) and the band is in top form on Good Lovin', Mason’s Children, High Time and a smoking Dark Star.  Recording quality is solid for a vintage soundboard tape – clear enough to enjoy despite some distortion, drop‑outs and a half‑step pitch slowdown noted by a few listeners.  Overall the performance is highly regarded, with the The Eleven sequence getting special praise while Hard To Handle is mentioned as unusually brief.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4‑5 stars and highlight strong musical moments; recording issues are noted but do not dominate, yielding a combined weighted score near 4.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Occasional distortion and drop‑outs, a half‑step slower tape speed in one copy, but overall clear and listenable; vintage tape hiss expected.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑'70 set builds nicely from tight, studio‑like Dire Wolf into a powerful second half highlighted by Dark Star and an especially compelling The Eleven sequence.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's guitar work is praised as part of the overall strong performance; no specific tonal commentary beyond general excellence.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil's bass is referenced in discussion about the difficulty of The Eleven, implying solid support on that challenging piece.
band_member_comments.Keys: The Hammond organ has a distinct '67 feel and was reportedly sourced from a Baptist church, giving the show a unique keyboard texture.
